title: Absorbing Data
coreMove: Convert raw information into shared knowledge by filtering, framing, and deciding what the pattern changes next.
sourcePressure: The chapter closes on turning information into knowledge in Cincinnati's public schools, making data absorption an interpretation and shared-understanding problem rather than a collection problem.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Believing more dashboards, reports, or numbers automatically create better understanding.

sourceAnchors.name: Cincinnati's public schools
sourceAnchors.detail: the subtitle directly supports Cincinnati's public schools as the institutional setting for turning information into knowledge
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Cincinnati's public schools should carry the scale of the problem: a system can collect signals and still need a shared read.

sourceAnchors.name: turning information into knowledge
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar allows this exact phrase as the chapter's central conversion problem
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Information becomes knowledge only when someone can say what the pattern means and what should change because of it.

sourceAnchors.name: public schools
sourceAnchors.detail: the source boundary permits public schools as the institutional anchor but not named administrators or program details
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The school setting should not become district gossip; it should show why shared interpretation matters when many people must act from the same signals.

hook: Person at a meeting realizes the real lesson
The day starts with a dashboard
counterintuition: Productivity is not doing more faster
The problem is not effort but something deeper

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a literacy nonprofit reviewing reading scores across after-school sites
exampleSpecs.audience: a program director facing twenty pages of mixed scores
exampleSpecs.stakes: funding and tutoring hours may go to the wrong site
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hannah cuts the report to one pattern by grade band, then asks what tutoring allocation must change this week
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Twenty pages of reading scores fan across the conference table

exampleSpecs.domain: a quality-control lab flooded with sensor readings from a cheese-aging room
exampleSpecs.audience: a food scientist trying to explain spoilage variation
exampleSpecs.stakes: an expensive batch may be discarded for the wrong reason
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marco ranks humidity swings against temperature and rind notes until the data points to one aging-room pattern
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The aging room smells of salt, milk, and damp wood shelves

exampleSpecs.domain: a city bike-share team reviewing repair tickets after stations empty too quickly
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations analyst with too many complaints and GPS traces
exampleSpecs.stakes: crews may keep rebalancing bikes without fixing the actual station pattern
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 9:22 a.m., Layla groups tickets by station behavior rather than complaint wording and finds the morning-transfer pattern
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 9:22 a.m., the station map shows red dots along one bridge approach

exampleSpecs.domain: a church finance committee interpreting donation changes after a building campaign
exampleSpecs.audience: a treasurer trying to avoid overreacting to one large gift
exampleSpecs.stakes: the committee could cut outreach based on a misleading total
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: James separates recurring gifts, one-time gifts, and campaign pledges so the committee discusses the pattern instead of the headline total
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "We are up eight percent," someone says, already smiling

exampleSpecs.domain: a ski patrol reviewing incident reports after three minor crashes on one slope
exampleSpecs.audience: a patrol supervisor deciding whether to change signage or staffing
exampleSpecs.stakes: the wrong fix could leave the real hazard unchanged
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Frida extracts time, snow condition, and turn location from each report until one pattern changes the patrol plan
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What do three separate crash reports know only when you read them together?
mustAvoid: letting the question hook replace the visible action beat

exampleSpecs.domain: a small manufacturer reading warranty returns across three product lines
exampleSpecs.audience: a plant manager buried in customer notes and defect codes
exampleSpecs.stakes: teams may chase the loudest customer complaint while missing the root pattern
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Pavel turn loose complaint notes into a shared one-page read, then change inspection around the defect cluster
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are holding a torn cardboard return box with three different defect codes

skillTargets: choose filtering and framing moves that create a shared read
evaluate whether a metric changes action or only adds noise

tryThisNowSpec: Take one report, chart, or note pile and write one sentence that answers: what pattern matters, and what next action changes because of it?
